1000/- Atrocities Act and in default of Payment of fine amount further R. I. for 1 year All the sentences were ordered to run concurrently.

Heard Mr. Jitendra Shukla, learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. H. S. Ahluwalia, learned Deputy Advocate General appearing for the State/respondent on the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail (IA No. 1 of 2023).

Prosecution story in brief is that in the year 2014-15, the three victim boys were Selected under tribal student scheme for admission in class-6 and the Tribal Department directed for admission in Vedanta Public School, Devendra Nagar, Raipur.
The parents of the said students contacted to proprietor of Vedanta Public School and handed over him their children for education.

Thereafter,
when the children came back to their home in vacation, they told their parents that the work of sweeping and mopping is done by the school proprietor and his wife in their house.

After knowing this, the father of the victim boys complained to the local MLA about the said fact and the MLA went to the school with media persons and the children were found to be hostage in the house of the accused.
Therefore the FIR has been lodged and the above said offence has been registered against the appellant.
Learned Counsel for the convict/appellant submits that the appellant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
He submits that there is a political motive to implicate the present applicant in the crime in question.

He also submits that from the statments of the victim boys i.e. PW-3 and PW-4 recorded before the trial Court, neither the specific date has been mentioned where the work of sweeping and mopping has been done by them nor the time has been mentioned.

He further submits that druing trial, the appellant was on bail but after his conviction he is in jail since 16.12.2022 and the appeal is likely to take a couple of years or even more for its final disposal, hence he prays that the appellant be enlarged on bail
The learned counsel for the State/respondent has objected the bail application.
However, he fairly submits that the appellant has no criminal antecedent.
We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records of the Court below.

Considering the facts & circumstance of the case particularly considering the fact that the victim boys have no where stated that on which date and time the work of sweeping and mopping has been done by them and further that the appellant is in jail since 16.12.2022, the appellant has no criminal antecedent and hearing of this appeal would take some time, we deem it appropriate to allow the application for suspension of sentence and grant of bail to the appellant.
